sentences.en: There's no time this lifespan...
sentences.zh: 在这个生命周期里，时间已经所剩无几了……

sentences.en: Pamela Hayes and Kristen Baer.
sentences.zh: 帕梅拉·海耶斯和克里斯汀·贝尔。

sentences.en: So thank you guys for being here today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢各位今天能来到这里。

sentences.en: And let's talk about lifespan integration.
sentences.zh: 我们来聊聊全距整合疗法（Lifespan Integration）。

sentences.en: How do you use lifespan integration?
sentences.zh: 你们是如何运用全距整合疗法的？

sentences.en: What brought you to it?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你们接触到它的？

sentences.en: And then maybe we can go over a brief history of it, not too academic.
sentences.zh: 也许我们可以简单回顾一下它的历史，不用太学术化。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I was brought to using lifespan integration just through my own healing journey.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我接触全距整合疗法完全是因为我自己的疗愈之旅。

sentences.en: It was something for me that was really helpful.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，它真的非常有帮助。

sentences.en: And my own therapist used it with me.
sentences.zh: 我的治疗师也曾对我使用过它。

sentences.en: So once I went through it and she told me that there was a training coming to Birmingham, then I jumped right in and have been using it with my clients ever since.
sentences.zh: 所以当我体验过之后，她告诉我伯明翰将有一场培训，我便毫不犹豫地加入了，从那以后一直在我的来访者身上使用它。

sentences.en: I find it to be a really helpful healing modality.
sentences.zh: 我发现这是一种非常有帮助的疗愈方式。

sentences.en: I use it with somatic experiencing and it's a body-focused modality.
sentences.zh: 我将它与躯体体验疗法（somatic experiencing）结合使用，这是一种以身体为核心的疗法。

sentences.en: So it really complements somatic experiencing and the work that I do with my clients.
sentences.zh: 所以它非常契合躯体体验疗法，以及我为来访者所做的工作。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, that's really just what brought me to it was my own healing through lifespan integration.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，真正让我接触到它的，就是我在全距整合疗法中获得的自我疗愈。

sentences.en: So I actually was looking to Kristen to consult about one of my clients because I knew she did the lifespan integration and somatic experiencing.
sentences.zh: 其实当时我是想向克里斯汀咨询我的一个来访者，因为我知道她做过全距整合和躯体体验疗法。

sentences.en: And so I was curious about some of that.
sentences.zh: 所以我对其中的一些内容很好奇。

sentences.en: And so I went and talked with her about one of my clients who I was thinking might really benefit from it just based on the few things that she had told me about lifespan.
sentences.zh: 于是我去找她谈了谈我的一位来访者，根据克里斯汀之前跟我讲过的一些关于全距的皮毛，我觉得这位来访者可能会从中受益。

sentences.en: And when we got to talking, it turned out that my client, for a reason, couldn't see her.
sentences.zh: 当我们聊起来的时候，结果发现因为某些原因，我的来访者无法找她咨询。

sentences.en: And I was like, well, maybe I could just get trained in LI and then I could do it with my client.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，也许我可以去接受全距整合培训，然后我就可以在我的来访者身上做了。

sentences.en: And so then I literally went back to my office and looked up lifespan integration.
sentences.zh: 于是我真的回到办公室查了一下全距整合疗法。

sentences.en: And there was a training that weekend.
sentences.zh: 那个周末刚好有一场培训。

sentences.en: The level one training was literally like four days after that.
sentences.zh: 一级培训就在那之后的四天左右。

sentences.en: And so I was like, I'm just going to go for it.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想，管他呢，我要去试试。

sentences.en: So I reached out to the trainer, Stephanie, and I signed up.
sentences.zh: 于是我联系了培训师斯蒂芬妮，并报了名。

sentences.en: I was like, hey, last minute, can you let me in?
sentences.zh: 我当时说，嘿，临时起意，能让我进去吗？

sentences.en: And she was like, of course.
sentences.zh: 她说，当然可以。

sentences.en: And that was like the beginning of my journey a year ago, March to March of 24.
sentences.zh: 这就是我这段旅程的开始，从去年3月到24年3月。

sentences.en: And now I've done all four trainings and I'm totally bought in.
sentences.zh: 现在我已经完成了全部四项培训，我彻底被它吸引了。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢它了。

sentences.en: You definitely speed ran it.
sentences.zh: 你绝对是按加速键学完的。

sentences.en: You were like in training every other weekend for a minute.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，你感觉每隔一个周末都在参加培训。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, I got the four done in a year.
sentences.zh: 我是说，对，我一年内完成了四项培训。

sentences.en: So it's good.
sentences.zh: 所以这很好。

sentences.en: It's good.
sentences.zh: 真的很好。

sentences.en: It's really good.
sentences.zh: 非常棒。

sentences.en: And then Pamela, what brought you into LI?
sentences.zh: 那么帕梅拉，是什么让你接触到全距整合疗法的？

sentences.en: What did you do first?
sentences.zh: 你最开始做的是什么？

sentences.en: Because you do a couple of things.
sentences.zh: 因为你涉猎好几个领域。

sentences.en: You do some somatic stuff in EMDR and how did you kind of get into it?
sentences.zh: 你做一些躯体疗法和眼动脱敏再加工（EMDR），你是怎么接触到这一块的？

sentences.en: I primarily use internal family systems, but I got into Lifespan also from talking to Kristen.
sentences.zh: 我主要使用内在家庭系统疗法（IFS），但我接触全距整合也是通过和克里斯汀聊天。

sentences.en: But more than just talking to her about it, I watched Kristen's transformation.
sentences.zh: 但不仅是听她聊起，我还亲眼目睹了克里斯汀的蜕变。

sentences.en: Not intentionally.
sentences.zh: 这不是故意的。

sentences.en: I wasn't sitting there like waiting to see.
sentences.zh: 我不是坐在那里等着看结果。

sentences.en: But I did kind of slowly notice Kristen gain more of a sense of self over time.
sentences.zh: 但我确实慢慢注意到，随着时间的推移，克里斯汀对自我的感知越来越强了。

sentences.en: And I didn't even really link it to LI until she told me more about it.
sentences.zh: 直到她跟我讲了更多细节，我才把这和全距整合联系起来。

sentences.en: And I was like, oh, that makes a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，哦，这太说得通了。

sentences.en: Like I just watched her kind of grow more into herself over time.
sentences.zh: 就像我看着她随着时间推移越来越能活出自我。

sentences.en: And it was over the span of like a year and a half.
sentences.zh: 那是在大约一年半的时间里发生的。

sentences.en: And I was like, okay, I need to know more about what this is and how to do this.
sentences.zh: 于是我想，好吧，我需要更多了解这到底是什么、怎么做。

sentences.en: And so I went to level one training.
sentences.zh: 所以我去参加了一级培训。

sentences.en: And, you know, you have your own, what are they called when we do the practice trainings?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你有自己的……我们做练习培训时那个叫什么来着？

sentences.en: Like while we're there.
sentences.zh: 就是我们在那里的时候。

sentences.en: The practicums?
sentences.zh: 实操练习吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, the little practicums where we have partners and we do it for each other in real time.
sentences.zh: 对，就是那种有搭档的小实操，我们在现实中为彼此进行练习。

sentences.en: And I mean, it was very powerful.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的非常有冲击力。

sentences.en: And so I decided to go on to level two and I love it.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定继续参加二级培训，我太喜欢它了。

sentences.en: I really love it.
sentences.zh: 我是真的很喜欢。

sentences.en: I've noticed a lot within myself and my own LI experience with my therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 我在自己身上以及我与治疗师进行全距整合的体验中，注意到了很多变化。

sentences.en: And it's kind of led me to want to continue doing it with my clients.
sentences.zh: 这促使我想继续在我的来访者身上使用它。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for going through y'all's history with it.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你们分享各自与它的渊源。

sentences.en: But I'd like to back up just a second in case people aren't terribly familiar with lifespan integration.
sentences.zh: 但我想稍微倒回一点，以防大家对全距整合疗法还不是很熟悉。

sentences.en: So when this is what's interesting, like when Taproot started, like we were, there's one other place that did brain spotting, like somewhere in Huntsville.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当“主根”（Taproot）刚成立的时候，我们……亨茨维尔还有另一个地方在做脑波点穴疗法（brain spotting）。

sentences.en: But I think she wouldn't even really do it.
sentences.zh: 但我猜她甚至不愿意真正去做。

sentences.en: Like I'd called and tried to ask and she didn't like the modality.
sentences.zh: 我曾经打电话去咨询过，但她并不喜欢这种疗法。

sentences.en: But when we opened, we kind of identified all of these brain-based medicines that were emerging.
sentences.zh: 但当我们开业时，我们梳理了所有当时正在兴起的基于大脑的疗法。

sentences.en: One of them was IFS.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是内在家庭系统疗法。

sentences.en: One of them was somatic experiencing.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是躯体体验疗法。

sentences.en: One of them was lifespan integration.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是全距整合疗法。

sentences.en: One of them was brain spotting.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是脑波点穴疗法。

sentences.en: And then one of them was QEG brain mapping, polyvagal stimulation.
sentences.zh: 还有QEEG脑电图地形图、多重迷走神经刺激。

sentences.en: And we also looked at like micronutrition a whole lot because I felt like the commercialization wasn't really there yet.
sentences.zh: 我们还大量研究了微量营养学，因为我觉得当时的市场商业化程度还不够高。

sentences.en: But the research was kind of saying these things were about to kind of be transformative.
sentences.zh: 但研究表明，这些东西即将带来颠覆性的变革。

sentences.en: And those are like the models that we really saw as like kind of the post-CBT paradigm that was going to grow.
sentences.zh: 这些就是我们真正看到的、将要发展的后认知行为疗法（CBT）范式的模式。

sentences.en: And so at that point, there weren't really any brain spotting people around.
sentences.zh: 所以在那个时候，周围真的没有什么做脑波点穴的人。

sentences.en: Now there's a ton.
sentences.zh: 现在到处都是了。

sentences.en: But if you look at things that are growing in therapy, I mean, LI is one of the big ones.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看治疗领域中不断发展的疗法，全距整合绝对是其中最重要的一种。

sentences.en: You know, I can't talk about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我甚至无法谈论它。

sentences.en: I've read the book.
sentences.zh: 我读过那本书。

sentences.en: But then when I talk to people about the book, they're LI trainers.
sentences.zh: 但当我跟别人谈起这本书时，他们都是全距整合的培训师。

sentences.en: Like they're like, no, no, no, don't read the book.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，不不不，别读这本书。

sentences.en: The book's actually so old that it's wrong now.
sentences.zh: 这本书其实太老了，现在已经不对了。

sentences.en: And LI is like this whole new thing.
sentences.zh: 全距整合现在完全是另一回事了。

sentences.en: And you have to do the training to know about it.
sentences.zh: 你必须亲自去参加培训才能了解它。

sentences.en: But, you know, Peggy Pace is the founder.
sentences.zh: 不过，佩吉·佩斯（Peggy Pace）是创始人。

sentences.en: And she invents it in the early 2000s, like 2001 or 2002.
sentences.zh: 她在2000年代初发明了它，大概是2001或2002年。

sentences.en: And then, you know, it's a collaborative thing.
sentences.zh: 然后，这是一个协作的成果。

sentences.en: There were tons of people kind of help her.
sentences.zh: 有许多人曾协助过她。

sentences.en: And she's like reflecting on the process.
sentences.zh: 她也在不断反思这个过程。

sentences.en: And it changes quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 它发生了相当大的变化。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of alchemization where, you know, like you figure out what's working and why it works.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个融合提炼的过程，你知道的，就像你要找出什么方法管用、为什么管用一样。

sentences.en: And then there's some techniques that are pretty different than what's going on in 2000 now.
sentences.zh: 因此，现在有些技术与2000年时的情况相当不同。

sentences.en: But it's a very vibrant, active community.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个充满活力、积极向上的社群。

sentences.en: I mean, when you meet LI people, they're not like, oh, yeah, I do LI.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当你遇到全距整合圈子的人时，他们不会那种：“哦，对，我做全距整合，我去拿个百吉饼吧”在会议上那种态度。

sentences.en: Let me get a bagel, you know, at the conference.
sentences.zh: 他们在会议上不会这样。

sentences.en: They're like really excited to talk to you about it.
sentences.zh: 他们是真的非常兴奋地想跟你聊这个。

sentences.en: And, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，

sentences.en: I think that it's one of the kind of emerging and growing models that does do this kind of brain-based trick to change the way that our brains perceive time and trauma and somatic energy,
sentences.zh: 我认为它是那些正在兴起和发展的模式之一，它确实运用了这种基于大脑的技巧，来改变我们的大脑感知时间、创伤和躯体能量的方式，

sentences.en: like all of the other kind of models that we do at Taproot, like the stuff that I like.
sentences.zh: 就像我们在“主根”所做的所有其他模式一样，也就是我喜欢的那类东西。

sentences.en: Even though I don't do it, I've seen that with patients.
sentences.zh: 尽管我不用它，但我从患者身上看到了这一点。

sentences.en: And I've also seen it have a different effect than when you do brain spotting.
sentences.zh: 我也看到它产生了与做脑波点穴时不同的效果。

sentences.en: I've seen people who do parts work, you know, internal family systems or voice dialogue or process-oriented therapy or something.
sentences.zh: 我见过有人做部分工作（parts work），也就是内在家庭系统疗法、声音对话（voice dialogue）或过程导向心理疗法之类的。

sentences.en: And then they also try LI and they're like, oh, this is what I got out of this and this is what I got out of that.
sentences.zh: 然后他们也尝试了全距整合，他们会说：“哦，这是我从这个里面得到的，这是我从那个里面得到的。”

sentences.en: You know, I see them kind of collaboratively benefit.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我看到他们从中获得了协同受益。

sentences.en: You guys are all kind of integrative practitioners.
sentences.zh: 你们大家都是整合型执业治疗师。

sentences.en: So could you say a little bit, you know, if somebody is a provider being like, why should I get trained in LI or a patient being like, why should I seek out an LI provider?
sentences.zh: 所以你们能不能稍微讲讲，如果有人是一个执业者，会想：“为什么我应该接受全距整合培训？”或者作为患者会想：“为什么我应该寻找全距整合治疗师？”

sentences.en: You know, how does this fit into like a bigger paradigm of healing?
sentences.zh: 这如何契合更宏大的疗愈范式？

sentences.en: You know, what does it do that is different than another kind of therapy that I do?
sentences.zh: 它所做的事情与我做的其他疗法有什么不同？

sentences.en: Or, you know, how does it fit into like a kind of bigger thing?
sentences.zh: 或者说，它如何融入某种更宏大的体系中？

sentences.en: You want to just kind of go in order from Marie, Kristen, Pamela, and then go through all those, the ways that you use it?
sentences.zh: 要不我们就按玛丽、克里斯汀、帕梅拉的顺序来，顺着把你们使用它的方式都讲一遍？

sentences.en: Because y'all are all different practitioners, you know, doing a model that is not standard, but, you know, it's a technique.
sentences.zh: 因为你们都是不同的执业者，在运用一种并非标准化、但却是一门技术的模式。

sentences.en: I'll turn it over to you.
sentences.zh: 我就把时间交给你了。

sentences.en: I lose video in my office all the time.
sentences.zh: 我办公室的视频总是掉线。

sentences.en: So, yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然可以。

sentences.en: I love using lifespan integration for a couple of reasons.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢使用全距整合疗法有几个原因。

sentences.en: So I was the first brain-based, brain-body-based medicine intervention, if you will, that I was trained in was brain spotting.
sentences.zh: 我接触的第一种基于大脑、脑体结合的医学干预手段，如果你愿意这么叫的话，是脑波点穴疗法。

sentences.en: And so I was really into that.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时非常沉迷于此。

sentences.en: And it was really awesome.
sentences.zh: 而且它真的很棒。

sentences.en: I'd seen some like great healing happen as a result of the brain spotting sessions that I did with clients.
sentences.zh: 我看到我与来访者进行脑波点穴疗程后取得了很好的疗愈效果。

sentences.en: And as Pamela was saying, too, even just in the trainings for brain spotting in the practicums, my own personal experiences were pretty great.
sentences.zh: 正如帕梅拉刚才所说，甚至在脑波点穴的培训和实操中，我个人的体验也非常棒。

sentences.en: And so I was definitely into that.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时确实深陷其中。

sentences.en: And I still am.
sentences.zh: 现在也是如此。

sentences.en: I still think it's a great tool.
sentences.zh: 我仍然认为它是一个伟大的工具。

sentences.en: But I will say that I have found that lifespan integration seems to be a lot more tolerable for some of a lot of my clients,
sentences.zh: 但我必须说，我发现对于我的许多来访者来说，全距整合疗法似乎更容易耐受，

sentences.en: because most of my clients have had severe lifelong complex trauma issues.
sentences.zh: 因为我的大多数来访者都有着严重、终身且复杂的创伤问题。

sentences.en: They've just really experienced a lot in their lifespan.
sentences.zh: 他们在各自的生命历程中确实经历了很多。

sentences.en: No point intended.
sentences.zh: 双关语，并非有意为之（Lifespan意为生命历程）。

sentences.en: And so with the brain spotting, you know, it can be very emotionally overwhelming for some people.
sentences.zh: 所以对于脑波点穴来说，你知道，对某些人来说可能会带来过度的情感重压。

sentences.en: And so I have found that with my clients that really did not tolerate brain spotting well, because I had a number of existing clients who had tried brain spotting and, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此我发现，对于那些对脑波点穴耐受度不佳的来访者——因为我有一些老客户尝试过脑波点穴，你知道的，

sentences.en: just weren't super comfortable with it.
sentences.zh: 就是感觉不太适应。

sentences.en: And then when I got trained in L.I., like right at the beginning, I just talked to my existing clients about it.
sentences.zh: 后来当我接受了全距整合培训后，在一开始，我就跟我的老客户们聊了聊这个。

sentences.en: And I was like, hey, you want to give this a shot?
sentences.zh: 我对他们说，嘿，你们想不想试试这个？

sentences.en: And they were all pretty much open to it.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上都持开放态度。

sentences.en: And so that was when I started to try it with people who had tried brain spotting before.
sentences.zh: 于是我就开始在那些以前尝试过脑波点穴的人身上尝试它。

sentences.en: And it definitely was received a lot better by some of my clients.
sentences.zh: 我的一些来访者对它的接受度确实好得多。

sentences.en: Some people still prefer brain spotting.
sentences.zh: 有些人仍然更喜欢脑波点穴。

sentences.en: There's just some differences.
sentences.zh: 它们只是一些细节上的差异。

sentences.en: But with the L.I., it's more of a gentle process, I think, is the way I often describe it.
sentences.zh: 但对于全距整合，我认为我通常会把它描述为一个更温和的过程。

sentences.en: Brain spotting can be a little bit more jarring, a little bit more, you know, overwhelming emotionally.
sentences.zh: 脑波点穴可能会更具冲击力，在情感上更让人难以招架。

sentences.en: Whereas in lifespan integration, the goal is always to get somebody into their window of tolerance and keep them in the window of tolerance.
sentences.zh: 而在全距整合中，目标始终是让来访者进入他们的耐受窗口（window of tolerance），并让他们保持在耐受窗口内。

sentences.en: So they're able to tolerate whatever emotional response is coming up.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就能承受任何浮现出来的强烈情感反应。

sentences.en: And so, you know, L.I.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，全距整合

sentences.en: is sort of a gentle re-networking of the neural network in the brain without re-traumatizing clients, which I think has been really great.
sentences.zh: 就像是对大脑中神经网络的一种温和的重新构网，而不会让来访者再度经历创伤，我认为这真的非常棒。

sentences.en: So we get to acknowledge the things that have happened in the past and reprocess them in a way that is similar to the brain and body-based treatments like brain spotting and EMDr.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们得以承认过去发生的事情，并以一种类似于脑波点穴和EMDR等脑体结合疗法的方式对它们进行重新加工。

sentences.en: But it just seems gentler, a softer path, if you will.
sentences.zh: 但它似乎更温和，可以说是一条更柔和的路径。

sentences.en: So that's all I got on that one.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，我要说的就是这些。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So, yeah, lifespan, it really complements a lot of therapy modalities.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，全距整合确实能与许多疗法模式完美互补。

sentences.en: I feel like you can use it with most clients.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你可以把它用在绝大多数来访者身上。

sentences.en: And like Marie said, a lot of my clients, they do have complex trauma.
sentences.zh: 就像玛丽说的，我的很多来访者确实都有复杂的创伤。

sentences.en: And the first stage of L.I.
sentences.zh: 而跨度整合治疗的第一阶段

sentences.en: therapy is about stabilization.
sentences.zh: 主要关于稳定化。

sentences.en: So it's really about building a really great foundation for doing some of the deeper work.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上是为进行一些更深层的治疗工作打下非常好的基础。

sentences.en: And it can create, it can help the client to expand their window of tolerance or have more capacity to be with some of the deeper rooted things that might come up.
sentences.zh: 并且它可以创造，它可以帮助来访者扩展他们的耐受窗口，或者有更多能力去面对一些可能会浮现的更深层次的根源问题。

sentences.en: And with lifespan, I mean, really, you can use it for trauma resolution.
sentences.zh: 而且对于跨度整合来说，我的意思是，实际上，你可以用它来解决创伤。

sentences.en: You can also use it to strengthen your core self, gain more insight into why you do the things you do, some of the behaviors you may have, the beliefs you may hold,
sentences.zh: 你也可以用它来强化你的核心自我，对你为什么做你所做的事情、你可能拥有的一些行为以及你可能持有的信念获得更多的洞察，

sentences.en: the strategies that you do to uphold those beliefs.
sentences.zh: 以及你用来维护这些信念的策略。

sentences.en: And so it's a really insightful therapy and something that I think differentiates it from some other modalities is the importance of attunement with the clinician.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种非常有洞察力的疗法，我认为它区别于其他一些疗法的一个重要之处就在于临床心理师需要具备同频共情（attunement）的能力。

sentences.en: So the clinician is an attuned, regulated presence for the client as they explore these different protocols.
sentences.zh: 因此，当来访者探索这些不同的治疗方案时，临床心理师对来访者来说是一个能够同频共情、情绪稳定的陪伴存在。

sentences.en: And our job is really just to hold the client, hold space for the client, give the client the experience of being cared for, held.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作其实就是承托来访者，为来访者包容空间，让来访者体验到被关怀、被承托的感觉。

sentences.en: We attune ourselves to our clients and notice, like, is our client within their window of tolerance?
sentences.zh: 我们将自己与来访者调频同频，并留意，比如，我们的来访者是否在他们的耐受窗口之内？

sentences.en: And then that informs us on how we do the protocols.
sentences.zh: 然后，这会指导我们如何开展治疗方案。

sentences.en: So we might increase pacing or use a certain number of memory cues.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能会加快节奏，或者使用一定数量的记忆提示。

sentences.en: And something else that's really beautiful about it is it's really based on attachment theory.
sentences.zh: 关于它，另一个真正美妙的地方在于它确实基于依恋理论。

sentences.en: So it really, you know, it's like with the knowledge that we all have the capacity to heal, that because we may have disorganized or avoidant attachment or anxious attachment,
sentences.zh: 所以它确实，你知道，就好像带着我们都拥有治愈能力的认知，尽管我们可能有混乱型依恋、回避型依恋或焦虑型依恋，

sentences.en: it doesn't mean that we have to have that attachment style forever.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着我们必须永远保持那种依恋风格。

sentences.en: We can actually move into a place of earned, secure attachment.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上可以进入一个获得安全型依恋的状态。

sentences.en: And that is the whole goal of lifespan integration therapy.
sentences.zh: 而这正是跨度整合疗法的全部目标。

sentences.en: So it's really just a beautiful modality, especially for those who have had attachment trauma.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的是一种非常美妙的疗法模式，特别是对那些有过依恋创伤的人来说。

sentences.en: And whenever I say trauma, I mean, a lot of us may even come into therapy thinking, well, I had a great childhood, you know,
sentences.zh: 每当我提到创伤时，我的意思是，我们中的许多人甚至在走进心理治疗时会想，嗯，我有一个很棒的童年，你知道的，

sentences.en: like I had clients or parents who provided good enough care.
sentences.zh: 就像我有提供足够好照顾的来访者或父母。

sentences.en: And trauma isn't always about what you didn't get.
sentences.zh: 而且创伤并不总是关于你没有得到的东西。

sentences.en: It's sometimes about, you know, the good things that didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 有时它是关于，你知道，那些没有发生的快乐美好的事情。

sentences.en: So we just use this modality really just to explore, explore the lifespan.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只是利用这种疗法模式来探索，探索生命历程。

sentences.en: And the whole basis of it is what's called the baseline timeline.
sentences.zh: 它的整个基础被称为基线时间线。

sentences.en: And it walks you through day one of your life all the way through present day.
sentences.zh: 它引导你从你生命的第1天一直走到现在。

sentences.en: And it grounds you in the safety of the present time.
sentences.zh: 它让你扎根于当下时刻的安全感中。

sentences.en: So that's really the goal of trauma therapy is to create more safety in the presence.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是创伤治疗的目标——在当下创造更多的安全感。

sentences.en: And that's what lifespan does.
sentences.zh: 这就是跨度整合疗法所做的事情。

sentences.en: We always end in present time.
sentences.zh: 我们总是以当下时刻结束。

sentences.en: So that's, that's just my take on it and how I use it with my clients.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我对此的看法，以及我是如何将它应用到我的来访者身上的。

sentences.en: And like I said before, I am trained in somatic experiencing.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前所说，我接受过躯体体验疗法的训练。

sentences.en: I've been through all the trainings and they complement each other so well because they're just both very, very gentle modalities.
sentences.zh: 我经历过所有的培训，它们相互完美互补，因为它们都是非常、非常温和的疗法模式。

sentences.en: Like Marie was saying, you know, it's, it's about not re-traumatizing.
sentences.zh: 正如玛丽所说，你知道的，这关键在于不造成二次创伤。

sentences.en: So not even having to live back through the trauma.
sentences.zh: 因此甚至不需要重新经历创伤。

sentences.en: A lot of clients don't want to have to talk about their traumatic experiences.
sentences.zh: 许多来访者不想去谈论他们的创伤经历。

sentences.en: And the beauty of lifespan integration is that they can just tell you a phrase and their brain is going to organize around the phrase that they're telling you.
sentences.zh: 跨度整合的美妙之处在于，他们只需要告诉你一个短语，他们的大脑就会围绕着他们告诉你的短语进行重组。

sentences.en: And it creates this reorganization of these neural networks that actually creates a lot more stabilization and peace in the client system.
sentences.zh: 它创造了这些神经网络的重组，这实际上在来访者的系统中创造了更多的稳定和平静。

sentences.en: And it's, it's, the benefits are, they're incredible.
sentences.zh: 而且它，它的益处是不可思议的。

sentences.en: I've seen it with my clients.
sentences.zh: 我在我的来访者身上看到了这一点。

sentences.en: And Pamela, can you talk about how that integrates with your work?
sentences.zh: 帕梅拉，你能谈谈这如何与你的工作相融合吗？

sentences.en: You may be one of the more parts-based people, similar to the, you know, I like the post-union stuff.
sentences.zh: 你可能是偏向基于内在部分的治疗师之一，类似于，你知道的，我喜欢后荣格学派的东西。

sentences.en: So that's what I'm doing.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我正在做的。

sentences.en: Can you talk maybe a little bit about how LI plugs into any of those kinds of parts-based structures?
sentences.zh: 你能稍微谈谈跨度整合如何融入任何这类基于部分的结构中吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's interesting because it pairs really well with IFS, particularly for clients who don't really want to talk a lot.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很有趣，因为它与内在家庭系统疗法（IFS）完美契合，特别是对于那些其实不想多说话的来访者。

sentences.en: And in IFS, there's also not a whole lot of talking, but lifespan is, is just so unique in that way.
sentences.zh: 在内在家庭系统疗法中，其实也没有太多对话，但跨度整合在这方面实在是太独特了。

sentences.en: Like Kristen said, like you can just offer a phrase.
sentences.zh: 就像克里斯汀说的，你可以只提供一个短语。

sentences.en: Um, and it really helps clients who struggle with overwhelm a lot because it,
sentences.zh: 嗯，它确实对那些饱受情绪压垮之苦的来访者有很大帮助，因为它，

sentences.en: it helps to resolve little pieces of emotion at a time versus kind of diving into any one particular trauma.
sentences.zh: 它有助于一次解决一小部分情绪，而不是一头扎进任何一个特定的创伤中。

sentences.en: So, um, well, and the other great thing about LI is it doesn't jump into somatic stuff, which is obviously where our trauma is, is in the body.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，好吧，跨度整合的另一个妙处在于它不会直接切入躯体方面，而我们的创伤显然正是在躯体中。

sentences.en: And so it doesn't treat somatic trauma, but you feel like how it doesn't, uh, jump into that.
sentences.zh: 因此它不治疗躯体创伤，但你觉得它是如何做到不，呃，直接切入那部分的呢？

sentences.en: Can you maybe parse that a little bit?
sentences.zh: 你能稍微剖析一下吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: Um, it starts like Kristen said, with building more of a foundation to where you can then, um, later on the, like the third stage,
sentences.zh: 嗯，就像克里斯汀说的，它从建立更多基础开始，到了解之后，呃，在稍后阶段，比如第三阶段，

sentences.en: I believe Kristen might be able to help me with this is when you start to go more into, um, what the body is actually holding.
sentences.zh: 我相信克里斯汀也许能帮我补充这一点——那时你开始更多地进入，呃，身体实际承载着什么。

sentences.en: But first it addresses things like how you've coped with the trauma, um, what beliefs you hold about yourself and others in the world.
sentences.zh: 但首先它解决诸如你如何应对创伤、呃，你对自已、他人以及世界持有怎样的信念等问题。

sentences.en: And once that safety is established, then you can go kind of deeper into where your body is holding all of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 一旦这种安全感建立起来，你就可以更深入地探讨你的身体在哪些地方承载着所有这些东西。

sentences.en: Kristen, can you help?
sentences.zh: 克里斯汀，你能帮补充一下吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: Um, yeah, I think stage two, stage three, or typically where we start to get more into the body for a lot of clients that come in, they're really in their heads.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，我认为第二阶段、第三阶段通常是我们开始更多地进入身体的阶段，对于许多进来的来访者来说，他们过多地停留在头脑里。

sentences.en: So that's where they over-intellectualize a lot, um, you know, kind of more dissociative.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他们过度理智化的地方，嗯，你知道的，有点更偏向解离状态。

sentences.en: And that's what makes a lie a really good, um, a good treatment for them is because,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么跨度整合对他们来说是一个非常好的，呃，非常好的治疗方法，因为，

sentences.en: you know, it can be like, okay, look, I know the body hasn't been a safe place for you to be.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它可以是这样的：‘听着，我知道身体对你来说一直不是一个安全的地方。’

sentences.en: So let's just start here, building more of a foundation, building up that window of tolerance.
sentences.zh: ‘所以让我们从这里开始，打牢基础，建立那个耐受窗口。’

sentences.en: We don't have to go into the body just yet.
sentences.zh: ‘我们现在还不需要进入身体。’

sentences.en: And then as you move toward the stage two of LI work, that's where you start to kind of pay more attention to the body sensations and the felt sense of what's coming up.
sentences.zh: 然后，当你走向跨度整合工作的第二阶段时，那就是你开始更多地关注身体感觉和浮现感受的时刻，

sentences.en: Um, as they hear there, these different protocols.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当他们听到这些不同的治疗方案时。

sentences.en: So you might notice like, Hey, you know, what are you noticing?
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会注意到，比如，‘嘿，你知道的，你注意到了什么？’

sentences.en: Do you notice tension?
sentences.zh: ‘你注意到紧张感了吗？’

sentences.en: Do you notice that you feel more relaxed when you hear this?
sentences.zh: ‘当你听到这个时，你有没有注意到你感觉更放松了？’

sentences.en: And often that comes up organically for clients.
sentences.zh: 通常这些会自然而然地为来访者呈现出来。

sentences.en: So, um, I even had a client last week who had been a little while since they had heard their timeline.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，上周我甚至有一个来访者，距离他们上次回顾时间线已经有一段时间了。

sentences.en: And once they heard the repetition of their timeline, they said, you know, gosh, that feels like such a relief.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们听到自己时间线的重复，他们就说，‘天哪，这感觉真是一种解脱。’

sentences.en: It's been, it's been a while, you know, I feel just like calmer.
sentences.zh: ‘已经有一段时间了，你知道的，我感觉平静多了。’

sentences.en: And that's often where we end our sessions.
sentences.zh: 而这通常是我们结束会话的方式。

sentences.en: We want to end our sessions where our client feels just a little bit better than they did when they came in.
sentences.zh: 我们希望结束会话时，来访者感觉比刚来时稍微好一点。

sentences.en: So that's really what we're monitoring as we do these protocols.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是我们执行这些方案时所监测的内容。

sentences.en: It's like with each repetition, after the timeline repetition, we take a break and it's, what are you noticing?
sentences.zh: 就像每次重复之后，在时间线重复完，我们休息一下，然后问：‘你注意到了什么？’

sentences.en: And sometimes that's, oh, I'm feeling more anxious or, oh, I'm feeling calmer.
sentences.zh: 有时那是：‘哦，我感到更焦虑了’，或者：‘哦，我感觉更平静了’。

sentences.en: So we just kind of, you know, go with that and then mold our treatment to the client.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只是，你知道的，顺其自然，然后根据来访者来调整我们的治疗。

sentences.en: And that's something else I think that differentiates, um, LI from a lot of therapy modalities is it's so customizable to our client's nervous systeMs.
sentences.zh: 这也是我认为将跨度整合与许多疗法模式区分开来的另一点，它是如此地可以针对我们来访者的神经系统进行定制。

sentences.en: Like we, when our clients come in for an intake, then we are assessing, you know, is this client, we have different types of clients, like type one, type two, type three.
sentences.zh: 就像我们，当我们的来访者进来进行初诊评估时，我们在评估，你知道的，这位来访者属于哪种类型，我们有不同类型的来访者，比如一型、二型、三型。

sentences.en: Um, and that's going a little deeper into some of the, the assessment piece, but we're kind of getting a sense of, okay, where is our client in their window of tolerance?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这稍微深入到了一些评估部分，但我们基本上是在感受：‘好的，我们的来访者在他们的耐受窗口的什么位置？’

sentences.en: Are they in the window of tolerance?
sentences.zh: ‘他们在这个耐受窗口内吗？’

sentences.en: Most of the time, none of the time, are they in more of a sympathetic state?
sentences.zh: ‘大部分时间，还是从来没有？他们更多地处于交感神经状态吗？’

sentences.en: A lot of the time are a parasympathetic state.
sentences.zh: ‘很多时间，还是副交感神经状态？’

sentences.en: Do we need to help up-regulate their nervous system, um, into the window or down-regulate the nervous system?
sentences.zh: ‘我们需要帮助提升他们的神经系统，嗯，进入窗口，还是下调神经系统？’

sentences.en: Like how can we create more, more ability and capacity to be within that window?
sentences.zh: ‘我们如何才能创造更多的能力和容纳度来呆在该窗口内？’

sentences.en: So, um, so yeah, we just mold these protocols to our clients and determine what it is that they need.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，所以是的，我们只是根据来访者调整这些方案，并确定他们需要什么。

sentences.en: And like I said, in the first stage, it's not about body.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，在第一阶段，它与身体无关。

sentences.en: We actually move through this pretty quickly and we're not trying to get into the body.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上非常迅速地度过这个阶段，而且我们并不是试图进入身体。

sentences.en: And so it makes it feel a little safer to some of our clients who are very much in their heads because the body hasn't been a very safe place to be.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于那些高度依赖头脑的来访者来说，这让他们感觉更安全一些，因为身体一直不是一个非常安全的存在之所。

sentences.en: And, um, one of the things that, um, I've seen when I hear people talk about lifespan is that, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，我听到人们谈论跨度整合时注意到的事情之一是，你知道的，

sentences.en: it's about a coherent life narrative that you're kind of using narrative as this way to get, uh, sort of like under a traumatic,
sentences.zh: 它是关于一个连贯的生活叙事，你某种程度上利用叙事作为一种方式来深入到，某种程度上像创伤事件的底层，

sentences.en: like event, but when a lot of people think of narrative therapy, they're thinking of the narrative,
sentences.zh: 但当许多人想到叙事疗法时，他们想到的是叙事，

sentences.en: the old school kind of like narrative therapy where there's a lot of journaling and you've got a big book and you have all the events with your life connected with strings on a board,
sentences.zh: 老派的那种叙事疗法，那里有很多写日记，你有一本大书，板上用线把你的生活中的所有事件连接起来，

sentences.en: or you do the tree where the fruit is the good stuff.
sentences.zh: 或者你画一棵树，树上的果子是美好的事物。

sentences.en: And the, these are the, the bad wounds that the tree grew around.
sentences.zh: 而这些是树绕着它生长的糟糕伤口。

sentences.en: And there's all these kinds of arts and crafts exercises, whereas LA doesn't quite work like that.
sentences.zh: 这里有各种各样的工艺美术练习，而跨度整合并不是完全那样运作的。

sentences.en: Um, it's a little bit more of making you experience your perception of time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它更多的是让你体验你对时间的感知。

sentences.en: Um, some of the stuff that I've heard patients tell me about their time in LA with other providers sounded almost like, um, like Ericksonian hypnosis, like parts of it,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我听患者向我讲述他们与其他提供者一起进行跨度整合的经历时，有些部分听起来几乎就像，嗯，像艾瑞克森催眠，某些部分类似，

sentences.en: where you're kind of like really encountering these earlier parts of self.
sentences.zh: 你有点像是在真正遭遇自我的这些早期部分。

sentences.en: Could you talk about the, the use of narrative to kind of transcend time, heal trauma in the practice of LA?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈在跨度整合的实践中如何利用叙事来超越时间、治愈创伤吗？

sentences.en: Anyone have any kind of reflections on that?
sentences.zh: 任何人对此有什么感想吗？

sentences.en: Um, yeah, I can.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，我可以。

sentences.en: So with the, the, um, as Kristen was kind of talking about, like, so we use timelines and, um, LA therapy.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如克里斯汀之前所谈到的，我们在跨度整合治疗中使用时间线。

sentences.en: And so it's not, it is a story of your life and it's kind of like, it's like watching a movie of your life.
sentences.zh: 所以它不是，它确实是你人生的故事，而且它有点像，就像观看你人生的电影。

sentences.en: Um, but we're kind of looking at highlight reels.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我们看的是精彩片段集锦。

sentences.en: So rather than trying to get every detail of your life experiences into one long consecutive story, um,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们不是试图将你生活经历的每一个细节都塞进一个漫长的连贯故事中，嗯，

sentences.en: we use what's called a timeline and the timeline is composed of what are called memory cues.
sentences.zh: 我们使用所谓的“时间线”，而时间线由被称为“记忆线索”的东西组成。

sentences.en: And so memory cues are one to a few words, um, that reminds somebody of a specific point in time, a specific memory, if you will.
sentences.zh: 因此，记忆线索是一到几个词，嗯，它能让人想起一个特定的时间点，如果你愿意的话，就是一个特定的记忆。

sentences.en: And so in building those timelines, the, the timeline is literally consisting of those, um, cues and not like additional information or, um, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，在构建这些时间线时，时间线字面意思上就是由这些，嗯，线索组成的，而不是附加信息，或者，你知道的，

sentences.en: more detail about the experiences, um, in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 关于过去经历的更多细节。

sentences.en: And so what happens is, um, for example, when we were doing the baseline timeline, like Kristen was talking about, um, so we would pick, um, we start with developmental cues.
sentences.zh: 所以发生的情况是，嗯，例如，正如克里斯汀所说，当我们制作基线时间线时，嗯，所以我们会选择，我们从发展线索开始。

sentences.en: So initially with the baseline timeline, you're starting with like, you're one day old.
sentences.zh: 所以最初制作基线时间线时，你是从你出生满1天开始的。

sentences.en: Um, so obviously we don't remember when we're one day old, but we believe and know that like the body and the brain have memory of that experience,
sentences.zh: 嗯，显然我们不记得自己1岁大时的情景，但我们相信并且知道，身体和大脑对这段经历是有记忆的，

sentences.en: even though you don't have like an explicit memory of it.
sentences.zh: 即使你对它没有外显记忆。

sentences.en: Um, so we start with developmental cues for those first days, first few years, um, because most people don't have explicit memories until around age two to four, two to three.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以对于前几天、前几年，我们从发展线索开始，因为大多数人在2到4岁、2到3岁之前都没有外显记忆。

sentences.en: Um, so then, um, from the first explicit memory or memory that somebody is able to consciously recall and tell themselves or others about, um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后，嗯，从第一个外显记忆或某人能够有意识地回忆并向自己或他人讲述的记忆开始，

sentences.en: we do at least one cue per year for the entire year or life.
sentences.zh: 我们为整个人生或每一年至少做一个线索。

sentences.en: Um, and then you can have up to three.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后你最多可以有三个。

sentences.en: So each year of the life can have, has to have at least one cue, um, and up to three, um, experiences that occurred in their life in that year of their life.
sentences.zh: 所以人生的每一年都可以拥有，必须至少有一个线索，并且最多可以有三个，嗯，记录在那一年生命中发生的经历。

sentences.en: Um, so, you know, if we've got somebody who's, you know, in their sixties, it is a longer timeline because we've got 60 years of experiences.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，如果我们有一个人，你知道的，已经六十多岁了，这是一个较长的时间线，因为我们有60年的经历。

sentences.en: Um, whereas naturally speaking, somebody who's younger, their timeline's gonna be a little shorter.
sentences.zh: 嗯，相比之下，自然而言，一个更年轻的人，他们的时间线就会短一些。

sentences.en: Um, but really it's just about including a variety of memories too.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但实际上它只是关于包含各种各样的记忆。

sentences.en: Um, so we, we kind of like to balance the story of the life without, with, um, you know, positive, negative, and neutral memories or cues.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我们，我们有点喜欢平衡人生的故事，融入积极、消极和中性的记忆或线索。

sentences.en: So we want to include, um, experiences that were very impactful and significant, um, so that those can start to be reprocessed.
sentences.zh: 所以我们希望包含，嗯，那些非常有影响力和意义的经历，以便这些经历可以开始被重新加工。

sentences.en: Um, and, but we also want to include just, you know, positive experiences in people's life.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，但我们也希望仅仅包含，你知道的，人们生活中的积极经历。

sentences.en: Like one of the ways that we can start to build that cohesive self, um, that Kristen was also talking about is identifying like the positive things that people have experienced.
sentences.zh: 就像我们开始构建那个有凝聚力的自我的方法之一，克里斯汀也谈到过，就是识别人们经历过的积极事物。

sentences.en: Especially when people who, you know, like we're working with predominantly have a lot of, a lot of, a lot of heavy stuff that they've been through.
sentences.zh: 特别是当我们合作的来访者，你知道的，主要都经历了很多、很多、很多沉重的事情时。

sentences.en: And that's, you know, uncomfortable or, you know, brings up uncomfortable feelings or emotions or thoughts.
sentences.zh: 而这，你知道的，让人感到不舒服，或者，你知道的，会唤起不舒服的感觉、情绪或想法。

sentences.en: You know, it's really nice to be able to incorporate, um, positive experiences.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，能够融入，嗯，积极的经历真的是一件很美好的事。

sentences.en: That's actually like one of the things I have on my treatment plans with my clients is like, if we're working on building, you know, an improved sense of self, um,
sentences.zh: 这实际上是我在与来访者的治疗计划中列出的内容之一，比如，如果我们正在努力建立，你知道的，一种得到改善的自我感，嗯，

sentences.en: raising self-esteem is tying in positive experiences, experiences where they were strong.
sentences.zh: 提升自尊心，那就是将积极的体验、他们表现坚强的体验串联起来。

sentences.en: And, you know, we're able to stand up for themselves or, you know, had good in our personal interactions, you know, just so we can get more of a balanced, um, story of the life.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们能够挺身而出维护自己，或者，你知道的，有着良好的人际互动，你知道的，这样我们就能获得更多平衡的，嗯，人生故事。

sentences.en: So that's, I mean, ultimately I think is the difference is, like I said, it's, it's specific points in time, not the entire story with all the details.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，归根结底我认为区别在于，正如我所说，它是特定的时间点，而不是包含所有细节的整个故事。

sentences.en: I will say too, the both, and I, I also, um, recipient as a client of LI.
sentences.zh: 我也想说，既……又……我也同时是，嗯，跨度整合治疗的来访者受益者。

sentences.en: And so like, as we're going through those timelines, more memories present.
sentences.zh: 所以，随着我们历经这些时间线，会有更多的记忆浮现。

sentences.en: Um, so one of the things that a lot of people will say when I explain lifespan integration is like, oh my gosh, I can't remember like what happened when I was 12.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因此，当我解释跨度整合时，许多人会说的一句话就是：‘天哪，我不记得我12岁时发生过什么了。’

sentences.en: How am I going to come up with a memory cue?
sentences.zh: ‘我该如何想出一个记忆线索？’

sentences.en: Well, we can use, um, certain points, um, in your life experiences that are pretty, a little bit more broad.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们可以使用，嗯，你生活经历中的某些点，它们相当，范围更广泛一些。

sentences.en: Um, so the ideal cue is going to be, like I said, a very specific moment in time that you can remember, but it can also be who your first grade teacher was,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以理想的线索将是，正如我所说，你可以记住的一个非常具体的时刻，但它也可以是你一年级老师是谁，

sentences.en: or that you lived in the yellow house.
sentences.zh: 或者你住在黄色房子里。

sentences.en: Um, because some people really aren't able to access more detailed memories for various reasons.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为有些人确实由于各种原因无法获取更多细节记忆。

sentences.en: Um, especially in times that were very traumatic for them, for their little systems to hold.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特别是在对他们的小系统来说非常具有创伤性的时期。

sentences.en: Um, and so that is also something we get to do is like, we can use more broad, but the timeline is always, it's a, I always say it's a flexible.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这也是我们能够做的事情，比如，我们可以使用更广泛的线索，但时间线始终是，我总是说它是一个灵活的。

sentences.en: Document.
sentences.zh: 文档。

sentences.en: It's a living document.
sentences.zh: 它是一个活的文件。

sentences.en: We can change it, update it.
sentences.zh: 我们可以更改它、更新它。

sentences.en: We can reword specific cues.
sentences.zh: 我们可以重新措辞特定的线索。

sentences.en: We can take out cues.
sentences.zh: 我们可以提取线索。

sentences.en: We can add cues, um, to really capture that full narrative of their life, um, in a way that is helpful to them.
sentences.zh: 我们可以添加线索，嗯，真正捕捉他们完整的人生叙事，嗯，用对他们有帮助的方式。

sentences.en: Um, and so that would just be like the thing too, is like that even if they don't remember something from a certain age or a certain time in their life,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这也是其中一点，就是即使他们不记得某个特定年龄或生命中某个特定时期的事情，

sentences.en: like usually hearing the timeline, um, and sessions and the repetitions that we do will start to expand some of those conscious memories, um,
sentences.zh: 比如通常听到时间线，嗯，还有会话以及我们所做的重复，会开始扩展其中一些有意识的记忆，嗯，

sentences.en: to bring more to their awareness as well.
sentences.zh: 从而将更多内容带入他们的意识中。

sentences.en: And, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，

sentences.en: one of the things that a lot of people bring up as part of what LA does is integrate different parts of self that you have different kind of extreme reactions or different extreme parts of self that don't get along or,
sentences.zh: 很多人提出的一点是，LIS所做的事情之一，就是整合你自身的不同部分，你有不同种类的极端反应，或者自我中不同的极端部分，它们合不来，或者，

sentences.en: or don't kind of see the value of each other.
sentences.zh: 或者看不到彼此的价值。

sentences.en: Um, Kristen, could you say anything about the way that you see that, um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，克里斯汀，你能谈谈你是如何看待这种，嗯，

sentences.en: integrate or, uh, the way that you see those parts of self sort of become more of a democracy and less of,
sentences.zh: 整合的，或者，呃，你是如何看待这些自我部分变得更像一个民主社会，而不是，

sentences.en: you know, pieces fighting for the wheel of a car and the van?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，各种碎片在争夺汽车和面包车方向盘的？

sentences.en: Um, you know, how do you see that, um, work and therapy?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，你是如何看待这种，嗯，治疗中的作用的？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, um, you know, they say about LA that it's about leaving ego states through time and often people do see like, oh, as I reflect on my life,
sentences.zh: 是的，嗯，你知道，关于LIS他们说的是，它是关于随着时间推移留下自我状态，人们确实经常看到，哦，当我回顾自己的一生时，

sentences.en: it feels like there's different versions of me that I've lived three different times, three different lives, you know?
sentences.zh: 感觉好像有不同版本的我，我经历过三次不同的时间，三段不同的人生，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And so people are able to reflect on that and kind of start to bring all of it together.
sentences.zh: 所以人们能够对此进行反思，并开始将所有这些结合在一起。

sentences.en: There's a lot of fragmentation that can happen over the course of someone's life and these parts of us that get stuck in these traumatic events or just in different times in our lives where there was something that happened,
sentences.zh: 在一个人的一生中，会发生很多破碎化，我们的这些部分被困在这些创伤事件中，或者只是在我们生命中发生过某些事情的不同时期，

sentences.en: like a parent's divorce or your own divorce or, you know, a car accident or something like that.
sentences.zh: 比如父母离异，或者你自己的离婚，或者，你知道，车祸之类的事情。

sentences.en: And so what we're doing is helping to connect all of these pieces together and create that more coherent life narrative.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正在做的是帮助把所有这些碎片连接在一起，并创造出更连贯的人生叙事。

sentences.en: And, you know, I tell my clients, it's like, imagine a jigsaw puzzle has just been thrown across the room and there's pieces here and there.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我告诉我的客户，这就像，想象一下拼图刚刚被扔满整个房间，这里一块，那里一块。

sentences.en: And we don't really have a coherent sense of self.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有真正连贯的自我感。

sentences.en: We don't really know, like, how did all these pieces connect and bring me to where I am now?
sentences.zh: 我们并不真正知道，比如，所有这些碎片是如何连接起来并将我带到现在的？

sentences.en: And so that's what we're doing, like piecing things together one at a time.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们正在做的，一次把事情一块块拼起来。

sentences.en: And as you create more coherence within the client system, then these parts start to kind of work more together.
sentences.zh: 当你在客户系统内创造更多的连贯性时，这些部分就会开始更多地协同工作。

sentences.en: So it's about the integration.
sentences.zh: 所以这是关于整合。

sentences.en: It's not about the separation of parts.
sentences.zh: 这不是关于部分的分割。

sentences.en: It's more about bringing them all together and creating a more solid core self.
sentences.zh: 这更多的是把它们全部聚集在一起，创造一个更坚实的内核自我。

sentences.en: And that's, you know, some of that work that we do where we are exploring these beliefs that people hold.
sentences.zh: 这就是，你知道的，我们所做的一些工作，我们去探索人们持有的这些信念。

sentences.en: You know, I tell people, you don't come into the world with these beliefs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我告诉人们，你来到这个世界时并没有这些信念。

sentences.en: They're imposed on you by some other, right?
sentences.zh: 它们是被别人强加给你的，对吧？

sentences.en: So we learn, like, what are these beliefs that we hold?
sentences.zh: 所以我们去了解，比如，我们持有的这些信念是什么？

sentences.en: Like, I'm unimportant or people can't hear me.
sentences.zh: 比如，我很重要或者人们听不到我的声音。

sentences.en: People don't understand me.
sentences.zh: 人们不理解我。

sentences.en: And we start to integrate these beliefs into the timeline and give people just more insight around them.
sentences.zh: 我们开始将这些信念整合到时间线中，让人们对它们有更多的洞察。

sentences.en: When did they start?
sentences.zh: 它们是什么时候开始的？

sentences.en: How did these things, when did I start believing this about myself?
sentences.zh: 这些事情，我从什么时候开始对自己有这种看法的？

sentences.en: And when are times that it's not necessarily true?
sentences.zh: 什么时候这些看法并不一定正确？

sentences.en: And strategies that we use to uphold these as well.
sentences.zh: 还有我们用来维护这些看法的策略。

sentences.en: Like, you know, I stay small and I stay quiet because others can't hear me.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道，我保持渺小，保持安静，因为别人听不到我。

sentences.en: And so it's really about these different parts of us that show up at different times that are protectors.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上是关于我们在不同时间出现的、作为保护者的不同部分。

sentences.en: And we get to know these protectors also through our timelines as well.
sentences.zh: 我们也会通过我们的时间线来了解这些保护者。

sentences.en: It's something we do in stage one.
sentences.zh: 这是我们在第一阶段做的事情。

sentences.en: And these protectors are often about things we're not doing.
sentences.zh: 而这些保护者通常与我们没有做的事情有关。

sentences.en: So maybe not connecting, not moving.
sentences.zh: 所以也许是不连接，不行动。

sentences.en: This is something that we start to gain more insight around, around how it's protected us throughout our life.
sentences.zh: 这是我们开始获得更多洞察的事情，关于它如何在我们的整个生命中保护了我们。

sentences.en: And we can form alliances with these protectors and these parts of ourselves that, you know, prevent us from being able to feel or prevent us from connecting with others.
sentences.zh: 我们可以与这些保护者以及我们自身那些阻止我们感受或阻止我们与他人连接的部分建立同盟，

sentences.en: And then we can also start to get a sense of how we've survived and those parts of us that have enabled that.
sentences.zh: 然后我们也可以开始了解我们是如何生存下来的，以及我们身上促成这一点的那些部分。

sentences.en: So it's really about forming alliances with the parts of ourselves and then bringing all the parts together into a more coherent whole, solid core self.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上是关于与自我的各个部分建立同盟，然后将所有的部分汇聚成一个更连贯、完整、坚实的内核自我。

sentences.en: And I mean, so the models of therapy that I tend to be more suspicious of are the ones that treat every person like they're the same or pretend like, well,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我往往更怀疑的治疗模型，是那种把每个人都当作一样对待的，或者假装认为，嗯，

sentences.en: once the provider has mastered this, then there's going to be this, if this, then that flow chart or formula for therapy.
sentences.zh: 一旦提供者掌握了这一点，就会有这种“如果……那么……”的治疗流程图或公式。

sentences.en: And then they get everybody to this place.
sentences.zh: 然后他们把每个人都带到这个地方。

sentences.en: The ones that I like a little bit more make a lot of room for the individuality and the subjectivity of the practitioner and the patient,
sentences.zh: 我更喜欢的那种，为从业者和患者的独特性和主观性留出了很大的空间，

sentences.en: because they are more of like a lens to examine an issue or, you know, a set of techniques wrapped in kind of a controlling metaphor or something.
sentences.zh: 因为它们更像是审视一个问题的镜头，或者，你知道的，包裹在某种控制性隐喻等之中的一组技术。

sentences.en: And there's a lot in lifespan.
sentences.zh: 在全寿命期中有很丰富的内容。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if you could talk to the flexibility of it.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能否谈谈它的灵活性。

sentences.en: Just going back to the influences, you know, I don't think Pace was influenced by Jung or any of the post-Jugians other than maybe Schwartz,
sentences.zh: 回到影响方面，你知道，我认为帕斯并没有受到荣格或任何后荣格学派的影响，除了施瓦茨之外，

sentences.en: because she doesn't seem to mention them.
sentences.zh: 因为她似乎没有提到他们。

sentences.en: Just the word ego states in the title of the first book makes me think about transactional analysis and Eric Byrne.
sentences.zh: 光是第一本书书名中的“自我状态”这个词，就让我想起了交互分析和埃里克·伯恩。

sentences.en: So that's probably sort of in the water that she's drinking.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能有点像她正在喝的水里本来就有的东西。

sentences.en: I would imagine never heard her mention that.
sentences.zh: 我想象她从未提到过这一点。

sentences.en: She does mention Schwartz and internal family system.
sentences.zh: 她确实提到了施瓦茨和内部家庭系统。

sentences.en: She talks about Dan Siegel's interpersonal neurobiology.
sentences.zh: 她谈到了丹·西格尔的人际神经生物学。

sentences.en: She talks about attachment theory, which some people use, you know, Balby and Ainsworth.
sentences.zh: 她谈到了依恋理论，有些人会用这个，你知道的，鲍尔比和玛丽·爱因斯沃斯。

sentences.en: And then memory reconsolidation theory.
sentences.zh: 然后是记忆再巩固理论。

sentences.en: The fact that, like, these memories are overwhelming and bad until we get a theta wave, until we can kind of go into them with more compassion, then they open up.
sentences.zh: 事实是，像，这些记忆是压倒性的、糟糕的，直到我们获得一个θ波，直到我们能够以更多的同情心进入它们，然后它们才会打开。

sentences.en: Now we're in a place where we can modify them, which is where therapy is supposed to happen.
sentences.zh: 现在我们处于一个可以修改它们的地方，这也是治疗应该发生的地方。

sentences.en: And then when they come back up, they're not as bad because it's about getting the trauma, not avoiding the trauma,
sentences.zh: 然后当它们再次浮现时，就没有那么糟糕了，因为关键在于正视创伤，而不是逃避创伤，

sentences.en: which I think cognitive therapy sometimes does or behavioral therapy can do.
sentences.zh: 我想认知疗法有时会这样做，或者行为疗法也可以做到。

sentences.en: But going into the trauma in a way that is useful in the therapy room so that when it comes up in life, it's not as bad.
sentences.zh: 而是以一种在治疗室中有用的方式进入创伤，这样当它在生活中出现时，就没有那么糟糕了。

sentences.en: And it seems like LA does that with playing with kind of narratives about time in a way like Ericksonian hypnosis and some of the older,
sentences.zh: 而且看起来LIS通过玩转关于时间的叙事方式做到了这一点，有点像埃里克森催眠和一些更古老的，

sentences.en: like I'm thinking of that Ericksonian hypnosis prompt about, you know, go back to your room when you're a child and think of the carpet on the ground.
sentences.zh: 就像我想起那个埃里克森催眠提示，关于，你知道的，回到你小时候的房间，想想地上的地毯。

sentences.en: And remember, you know, think of the doorknob and what the wood smelled like and open the door and see yourself on the bed as a kid.
sentences.zh: 记住，你知道，想想门把手和木头的气味，然后打开门，看到你自己作为一个孩子躺在床上。

sentences.en: A lot of the techniques that I've heard seem similar to those things where you're taking, you know, this piece of you has to be this thing.
sentences.zh: 我听过的大多数技术似乎都类似于这些东西，你把，你知道的，你这一部分必须是这个东西。

sentences.en: But at another time, this piece of you had to be that thing.
sentences.zh: 但在另一个时间，你这一部分必须是那个东西。

sentences.en: Now mush them together and make them fight and make them kind of figure out what the core self is.
sentences.zh: 现在把它们揉合在一起，让它们打架，让它们弄清楚核心自我是什么。

sentences.en: You know, that seems to be the experience of patients that I've heard that have also come to me for another kind of therapy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这似乎是我所听到的那些为了另一种治疗而来到我这里的患者的体验。

sentences.en: Anything about just the flexibility of this modality and how it kind of can hook into, you know, anybody's style, anybody's way of thinking?
sentences.zh: 关于这种疗法的灵活性，以及它如何能够融入，你知道的，任何人的风格、任何人的思维方式，有什么想说的吗？

sentences.en: Well, one of the things that, as you were talking just now, that came up for me or what I was thinking is that although LI is pretty, what's the word, structured, regimented,
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如你刚才在说话时，浮现在我脑海里或我正在想的一件事是，尽管LIS相当，怎么说呢，结构化，有条不紊，

sentences.en: like there are protocols, there is a direction for how you use the protocols, a progression of using the different protocols.
sentences.zh: 就像有协议一样，如何使用协议有指导方向，使用不同协议有一个发展过程。

sentences.en: But that being said, it is very much individualized per client as far as like, like Christa mentioned, the attunement piece.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，对于每个客户来说，它在很大程度是个性化的，就像克里斯塔提到的调谐部分。

sentences.en: So a lot of what we do as LI therapists is be attuned to what our client system needs in that session that day.
sentences.zh: 所以，作为LIS治疗师，我们做的很多事情都是去调谐我们的客户系统在那天该会话中需要什么。

sentences.en: As clients seem to progress in LI therapy and get later on to like stage two and stage three work,
sentences.zh: 随着客户似乎在LIS治疗中取得进展，并进入后期如第二阶段和第三阶段的工作，

sentences.en: they can be more collaborative in the process of, you know, identifying what is coming up for them, what their system is kind of telling them this week.
sentences.zh: 他们在合作过程中可以更加积极，你知道的，确定什么对他们来说浮现了，他们的系统本周在告诉他们什么。

sentences.en: But initially, we do a lot of that sort of attuning to them and identifying what they might benefit from.
sentences.zh: 但最初，我们会做很多对他们进行调谐并确定他们能从中受益什么的工作。

sentences.en: So doing different protocols, like Christa was talking about, the protectors.
sentences.zh: 所以要做不同的协议，就像克里斯塔谈到的那样，保护者。

sentences.en: And then we also have strategies, like things that we do to cope that we can sort of sense for the client.
sentences.zh: 然后我们也有策略，比如我们为了应对而做的事情，我们可以为客户感知到。

sentences.en: We kind of know where they are in their processing of their life experiences and what might be beneficial for them to do next.
sentences.zh: 我们有点知道他们处于处理生活经验的什么阶段，以及接下来对他们做什么可能是有益的。

sentences.en: So often, before they come in for their session, we're actually looking at what work we've done with them, where we went last,
sentences.zh: 所以通常，在他们来参加会话之前，我们实际上是在查看我们对他们做了什么工作，我们上次去了哪里，

sentences.en: and what might be a good direction to go in that session that day.
sentences.zh: 以及那天会话中什么可能是一个好的发展方向。

sentences.en: And then too, even once, you know, we may have a game plan, but once they enter into our office and they give us some feedback about, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且即使，你知道，我们可能有一个总体规划，但一旦他们进入我们的办公室并给我们一些反馈，关于，你知道的，

sentences.en: what is their system experience since their last session, we might even, you know, pivot and change the game plan a little bit.
sentences.zh: 自上次会话以来他们的系统体验是什么，我们甚至可能会，你知道，稍微调整和改变总体规划。

sentences.en: So it really is about, like, attuning to what it is that they need in that moment.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是关于，比如，调谐到他们在那个时刻需要什么。

sentences.en: But also, like, I do appreciate that there is a structure to it.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我也很欣赏它确实有结构。

sentences.en: There's very much a path to how we proceed through the different protocols.
sentences.zh: 我们如何通过不同的协议推进，是非常有路径可循的。

sentences.en: And protocols, I'm mentioning, are just different timelines, different types of timelines.
sentences.zh: 我提到的协议，只是不同的时间线，不同类型的时间线。

sentences.en: So we've talked about, like, the baseline timeline, which is, like, the story of the entire life.
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论过，比如，基线时间线，也就是整个生命的故事。

sentences.en: And then we have protocols for specific traumas, like a PTSD timeline or what we call a TLEM or timeline from explicit memory.
sentences.zh: 然后我们针对特定创伤有协议，比如PTSD时间线，或者我们称之为TLEM或来自外显记忆的时间线。

sentences.en: And so those are both used pretty early on in LI therapy to sort of clear out, if you will, anything that's happened or occurred in the past five years
sentences.zh: 因此，这两者在LIS治疗的早期都被广泛使用，可以说是为了清理在过去五年中发生的、

sentences.en: that feels unresolved or still brings up very strong emotions or maybe symptoms of PTSD around reminders or stimuli related to those events.
sentences.zh: 感觉未解决的、或者仍然唤起强烈情绪的任何事情，或者围绕对这些事件的提醒或刺激的PTSD症状。

sentences.en: And so the PTSD protocol is great because we can walk through, hit the high notes of an entire experience from the beginning to end and then bring them to present time.
sentences.zh: 所以PTSD协议非常棒，因为我们可以经历整个体验的最高潮，从头到尾，然后将他们带到现在。

sentences.en: But also the TLEM, that explicit memory timeline, is very helpful because it is even gentler
sentences.zh: 而且TLEM，那个外显记忆时间线，也非常有用，因为它甚至更温和，

sentences.en: where we just use one cue that connects back to the event at the very end of the event, sort of like where there was an assumed level of safety.
sentences.zh: 我们只使用一个线索，在事件的最后连接回事件本身，有点像在事件结束时存在一定程度的安全感的地方。

sentences.en: Like, they were able to feel some sense of safety towards the end of the event and then just bring them to the present time of cues.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们在事件快结束时能够感受到某种安全感，然后只需将他们带到当前的线索中。

sentences.en: So just to throw in there a couple of protocols that we do.
sentences.zh: 所以只是顺便提及我们所做的几个协议。

sentences.en: And then there are things that we can do later on in LI therapy.
sentences.zh: 然后还有我们在LIS治疗后期可以做的事情。

sentences.en: Once there's more like emotional regulation, distress tolerance, more core self-built, where we can actually go back into, you know,
sentences.zh: 一旦有了更多像情绪调节、痛苦耐受、建立更多内核自我，我们就可以真正回到，你知道的，

sentences.en: specific memories or experiences earlier in life.
sentences.zh: 生命中更早的特定记忆或体验中。

sentences.en: And so, you know, I think definitely with like, it is, you know, largely based around attachment theory.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为绝对像，它很大程度上是基于依恋理论。

sentences.en: And that's what I love.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所喜欢的。

sentences.en: I like I've ever since I heard about attachment theory, like that's just really what I clung to.
sentences.zh: 自从我听说依恋理论以来，这就是我真正紧紧抓住的东西。

sentences.en: I really believe it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很相信它。

sentences.en: But I think there's no way that we can really go through our lives expecting or believing that what we've been through in the past didn't shape us or impact us.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们绝不可能经历我们的人生，却期望或相信我们在过去经历的事情没有塑造我们或影响我们。

sentences.en: And so I've always wanted to help people work on, you know, identifying what are those things and how can we readdress or how can we read, read network, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我一直想帮助人们致力于，你知道，确定这些事情是什么，以及我们如何重新解决或如何重新建构网络，你知道，

sentences.en: rearrange general network to help no longer experience, you know, triggers related to our past experiences.
sentences.zh: 重新安排一般网络，以帮助不再体验到与我们过去经历相关的触发因素。

sentences.en: Which I think is very much, you know, how LI, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常符合，你知道，LIS是如何，你知道的，

sentences.en: operates is that these things that we have experienced across our lifespan are just so impactful and so important that they can't be ignored.
sentences.zh: 运作的，即我们在整个生命历程中所经历的这些事情是如此具有影响力且如此重要，以至于它们不能被忽视。

sentences.en: They need to be integrated.
sentences.zh: 它们需要被整合。

sentences.en: There are so many pieces, like if you think of it, like there are just pieces hanging out in different, you know,
sentences.zh: 有这么多的碎片，如果你这样想，就像有碎片悬挂在不同的，你知道，

sentences.en: areas and we're sort of bringing them all together to like build a cohesive network.
sentences.zh: 区域，而我们有点把它们全部聚集在一起，以建立一个有凝聚力的网络。

sentences.en: Like we said, with like the whole story of the life is being able to be held at the same place together.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，整个人生故事能够在同一个地方被共同容纳。

sentences.en: And so I really appreciate that because I always believed, like I said, in attachment theory and I really wanted a way to help people heal from childhood wounds.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很感激这一点，因为正如我所说，我一直相信依恋理论，我真的很想找到一种方法来帮助人们从童年创伤中治愈。

sentences.en: And this is exactly what LI has provided me with the opportunity to do.
sentences.zh: 这正是LIS为我提供的机会。

sentences.en: Yeah, and to expand on that, Marie, it's, you know, I think something that I really love about LI is that it really, it does honor the client's autonomy.
sentences.zh: 是的，为了对此进行扩展，玛丽，我认为我真的很喜欢LIS的一点是，它确实，它确实尊重客户的自主权。

sentences.en: So the client does have a say and they can choose how much that they share with us and what they want to work on.
sentences.zh: 所以客户确实有发言权，他们可以选择与我们分享多少以及他们想做什么。

sentences.en: And we, as the attuned clinicians, you know, we kind of gain a sense and we got our clients along the way,
sentences.zh: 而我们，作为调谐的临床医生，你知道，我们有一种感觉，我们在这一过程中引导我们的客户，

sentences.en: but as they progress through the stages of LI therapy and they gain more insight and they are able to be more assertive and know what it is that they need.
sentences.zh: 但随着他们经历LIS治疗的各个阶段，他们获得了更多的洞察力，并且能够更加自信，知道自己需要什么。

sentences.en: And they are able to kind of say, hey, yeah, I think that this is what I need today.
sentences.zh: 他们能够说，嘿，是的，我想这就是我今天需要的。

sentences.en: And then they can become more involved in the process.
sentences.zh: 然后他们可以更多地参与到这个过程中。

sentences.en: And, you know, I just think because it's so client centered and adaptable to every single client that we have, it's not just a, you know, one size fits all approach.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我只是认为因为它如此以客户为中心，并且适应我们的每一个客户，它不只是一个“一刀切”的方法。

sentences.en: We can, you know, come in and sit and hold space for our clients and kind of get a sense of what it is that they need and until they're able to do that on their own.
sentences.zh: 我们可以，你知道，进来坐着，为我们的客户提供空间，并了解他们需要什么，直到他们能够自己做到这一点。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I think it's a really beautiful modality and that it can be adapted in any way that it's needed for each client and you can use certain protocols and, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我认为这是一种非常美丽的疗法，它可以根据每个客户需要的任何方式进行调整，你可以使用某些协议，你知道，

sentences.en: not go through all the stages of LI therapy.
sentences.zh: 而不必经历LIS治疗的所有阶段。

sentences.en: If that's not what's right for the client at the time, you can resolve relationship wounds with relationship protocol.
sentences.zh: 如果这当时对客户来说不是正确的，你可以用关系协议来解决关系创伤。

sentences.en: You can work on PTSD events with the PTSD protocol.
sentences.zh: 你可以用PTSD协议来处理PTSD事件。

sentences.en: You can, you know, just work on forming these alliances with the protectors, with, you know, adding in some baseline pluses and just giving the client a general sense of, yeah,
sentences.zh: 你可以，你知道，只是致力于与保护者建立这些同盟，通过，你知道，添加一些基线加分项，并给客户一个普遍的感觉，是的，

sentences.en: this is my life and this is what has happened.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的生活，这就是发生的事情。

sentences.en: And it's led me to where I am now.
sentences.zh: 它把我带到了我现在的状态。

sentences.en: And now I am here and I am safe where I'm at now.
sentences.zh: 现在我在这里，在我现在所在的地方我很安全。

sentences.en: And, yeah, a lot of negative things have happened, but also a lot of positive things have happened.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，发生了很多消极的事情，但也发生了许多积极的事情。

sentences.en: And overall, like, I've survived.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，比如，我活了下来。

sentences.en: I'm here.
sentences.zh: 我在这里。

sentences.en: And that's really what I hear, you know, a lot from my clients is like, oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 这确实是我听到的，你知道，我的客户经常说的，就像，哦，哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like, I, we're really, really good at orienting toward the negative.
sentences.zh: 就像，我，我们真的，真的很擅长偏向消极。

sentences.en: You know, in SD, we call it the trauma vortex.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在SD中，我们称之为创伤涡流。

sentences.en: It has a very strong pull.
sentences.zh: 它具有非常强的吸引力。

sentences.en: And we often really want to focus on these negative things because that's what keeps us safe, right?
sentences.zh: 我们通常真的很想专注于这些消极的事情，因为这能让我们保持安全，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, if we're hypervigilant and we are aware of the negatives, then we can avoid those things or we can protect ourselves from those things.
sentences.zh: 就像，如果我们处于高度警觉状态，并且我们意识到了负面因素，那么我们就可以避免这些事情，或者我们可以保护自己免受这些事情的伤害。

sentences.en: And so, what we want to do in building capacity is build more capacity to be with the joy, be with the good things that have happened.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们在建立容量时想要做的是，建立更多的容量去与喜悦共存，去与发生的那些美好的事情共存。

sentences.en: And so, that does help to integrate both of those things.
sentences.zh: 所以，这确实有助于将这两件事整合起来。

sentences.en: Like, yeah, these bad things have happened, but look at how I survived it.
sentences.zh: 就像，是的，这些糟糕的事情发生了，但看看我是如何活过来的。

sentences.en: Look at how I'm still here.
sentences.zh: 看看我是怎么依然站在这里的。

sentences.en: Look at these really intelligent ways that my nervous system adapted to keep me safe and keep me alive.
sentences.zh: 看看我的神经系统为了保护我和让我活下来，所做出的那些真正聪明的调整。

sentences.en: And, you know, maybe now that I'm an adult, I don't need these things that I used to do, these strategies anymore.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，也许现在我长大了，我不再需要以前做的这些事情，这些策略了。

sentences.en: Maybe I can start to connect to others.
sentences.zh: 也许我可以开始与他人建立连接。

sentences.en: Maybe I can, you know, start to feel again.
sentences.zh: 也许我可以，你知道，开始去感受。

sentences.en: Maybe I can start to feel more in my body because I am in a different place now than I was when I was six years old.
sentences.zh: 也许我可以开始更多地感受自己的身体，因为我现在所处的地方与我六岁时不同了。

sentences.en: And I grew up in a really abusive household and not connecting and not feeling really helped keep me safe.
sentences.zh: 我在一个经常虐待的家庭中长大，不连接和不感受确实帮我保全了安全。

sentences.en: And so, that's the beauty of LI work is, you know, getting a sense of what are these adaptations that our nervous systems have made to keep us safe, to protect us.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是LI（神经整合）工作的奇妙之处，你知道的，去了解我们的神经系统为了保护我们做出了哪些调整。

sentences.en: And how can that change to fit our life now?
sentences.zh: 以及这如何改变以适应我们现在的生活？

sentences.en: Well, so I guess before we wrap up, I just want to throw out, you know, that this really has been really a life-changing modality for myself and for my clients.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想在结束之前，我只想说，这对我自己和我的来访者来说，确实是一种改变生活的方式。

sentences.en: As I've been in LI therapy for a while now, I have really experienced a lot of things shift and move for me and reactions that I don't have that I used to have.
sentences.zh: 随着我进行LI治疗有一段时间了，我真的体验到了许多事情的转变和流动，以及我不再有以前那种反应了。

sentences.en: Things that used to, what have really jarred me emotionally or really, you know, been heavy for me really aren't.
sentences.zh: 那些过去真正让我情绪崩溃或让我觉得沉重的事情，现在真的不算什么了。

sentences.en: I'm able to sort of acknowledge and recognize, you know, other key people in my life.
sentences.zh: 我能够某种程度上承认并认出，你知道，我生命中的其他关键人物。

sentences.en: Whereas in the past, something they said or did might put me on edge and make me really uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 而在过去，他们说的话或做的事可能会让我如坐针毡，让我非常不舒服。

sentences.en: And today, I can honestly say that, like, I'm able to recognize those things as having occurred and that those people, you know,
sentences.zh: 而今天，我可以诚实地说，就像，我能够认识到那些事情已经发生，而那些人，你知道，

sentences.en: their perceptions of the experience is that it's theirs.
sentences.zh: 他们对经历的看法是他们自己的。

sentences.en: It's not mine and I don't have to hold on to it and I don't have to carry it out.
sentences.zh: 那不是我的，我不需要抓住它，我也不需要把它背负下去。

sentences.en: And it's really just been a beautiful process of getting to learn myself and know myself and identify, like, who I am and, you know, what I get to do with my life moving forward.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一个美好的过程，去了解自己、认识自己，并明确我是谁，你知道，我接下来要如何过我的人生。

sentences.en: The things I have experienced do not have to define me moving forward.
sentences.zh: 我经历过的事情不必定义我未来的生活。

sentences.en: And also, I just wanted to add just one quick story.
sentences.zh: 另外，我只想补充一个简短的故事。

sentences.en: You know, I had a client who had done some LI work and witnessed an accident.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我有一个来访者做过一些LI工作，并且目睹了一场事故。

sentences.en: And so, this person had been traveling to work on the way past this accident scene every day.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个人每天上下班都会经过这个事故现场。

sentences.en: And we talked about it one session after the accident happened.
sentences.zh: 事故发生后的一节课上我们谈到了这件事。

sentences.en: And then the week after that, we actually did a PTSD timeline for that accident.
sentences.zh: 在那之后的第二个星期，我们实际上为那起事故做了一个创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）时间线。

sentences.en: And the client had been telling me literally that they were dreading passing that spot on the road for, you know, miles before they got there.
sentences.zh: 这位来访者 literalmente（字面意思）告诉我，他们在到达那个路口前几英里就开始害怕经过那里了。

sentences.en: And then following the PTSD timeline, they let me know in the next session that they had literally driven past the spot before they realized they passed the spot, I think,
sentences.zh: 然后做完PTSD时间线后，他们在下一次会谈中告诉我，他们开车经过那个地点时，甚至在开过去之后才意识到自己已经过了那个地方，我想，

sentences.en: which is really telling to the power of this therapy.
sentences.zh: 这真的很说明这种疗法的力量。

sentences.en: So, that's what I have.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我要分享的。

sentences.en: Kristen, anything you want to add before we wrap up?
sentences.zh: 克里斯汀，在我们结束之前有什么想补充的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I've had many similar client experiences.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是说，我有过很多类似的来访者体验。

sentences.en: It's really remarkable having clients come in and say, you know, I've had nightmares my entire life.
sentences.zh: 看到来访者走进来对我说，你知道，我一辈子都在做噩梦，这真的很了不起。

sentences.en: And since we started this therapy, I'm no longer having nightmares.
sentences.zh: 自从我们开始这种疗法以来，我不再做噩梦了。

sentences.en: I'm no longer having flashbacks.
sentences.zh: 我不再有闪回了。

sentences.en: I even have my own experience where I was in a car accident and had so much anxiety around driving.
sentences.zh: 我甚至有我自己的经历，我曾遭遇车祸，对开车产生了极大的焦虑。

sentences.en: And I was constantly checking my rearview mirror, like, is someone about to crash into me?
sentences.zh: 我经常查看后视镜，比如，是不是有人要撞上我？

sentences.en: And after doing LI protocols, like, notice, like, okay, I'm not feeling that whenever I'm driving anymore.
sentences.zh: 在做了LI方案后，就像，注意到，好吧，我开车时不再有那种感觉了。

sentences.en: And so, having experienced the power of LI myself, and as Pamela said, just, like, noticing my transformation over time,
sentences.zh: 所以，亲自体验了LI的力量，正如帕梅拉所说，只是注意到随着时间的推移我的转变，

sentences.en: has really proven to me just how effective this modality is.
sentences.zh: 真的向我证明了这种疗法有多么有效。

sentences.en: And it's what has driven me to, you know, go through all the trainings, move towards certification.
sentences.zh: 这也是促使我完成所有培训、走向认证的原因。

sentences.en: And I really love that LI to move towards certification requires their therapists to actually go through it themselves.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢LI走向认证的要求，那就是治疗师必须自己亲自体验过。

sentences.en: So, you know, we are doing the work alongside our clients.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们在和来访者一起做这项工作。

sentences.en: We are not perfect human beings.
sentences.zh: 我们不是完美的人类。

sentences.en: We have our own trauma.
sentences.zh: 我们也有自己的创伤。

sentences.en: It's really what led us to this work.
sentences.zh: 这正是引导我们从事这项工作的原因。

sentences.en: And the healing that we've done around it is what allows us to hold space and really understand what it is that our clients are going through.
sentences.zh: 我们围绕它所做的疗愈，正是让我们能够容纳空间并真正理解来访者正在经历什么的原因。

sentences.en: And so, in doing the LI work ourselves, you know, we're also able to be like, yeah, you know, like, this is tough work, but it's also really beautiful.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我们自己做LI工作的过程中，你知道，我们也能够说，是的，你知道，这工作很难，但它也很美好。

sentences.en: And it's challenging in a very gentle way.
sentences.zh: 而且它以一种非常温和的方式具有挑战性。

sentences.en: And I'm here, and I'm going to hold space for you, and we're going to get through this together.
sentences.zh: 我就在这里，我会为你容纳空间，我们会一起度过难关。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, LA, I mean, I believe in the power of it.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，LI，我是说，我相信它的力量。

sentences.en: It's been transformational for me, and I've witnessed the transformation in many of my clients.
sentences.zh: 它对我是变革性的，我也见证了许多来访者的转变。

sentences.en: And it's just amazing.
sentences.zh: 这简直太神奇了。

sentences.en: I will share a personal anecdote real quick before we go, because I haven't done quite as much work with my clients, but I've had a lot of it with my, you know,
sentences.zh: 在我们结束之前，我快速分享一个个人轶事，因为我没有和我的来访者做过那么多工作，但我从我的，你知道，

sentences.en: with my own therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 我自己的治疗师那里体验过很多次。

sentences.en: And there was one protocol in particular that we did, because I had a big presentation coming up.
sentences.zh: 有一个特定的方案我们做了，因为我有一个重要的演讲要进行。

sentences.en: It was a webinar, and it ended up being 1,200 people that were there.
sentences.zh: 那是一个网络研讨会，最后有1,200人参加。

sentences.en: And I have struggled with public speaking my entire life.
sentences.zh: 我一生都在与公开演讲作斗争。

sentences.en: It's been a really stuck point in my life ever since I can remember.
sentences.zh: 从我有记忆以来，这一直是我生命中一个真正卡住的点。

sentences.en: And we did a protocol before the presentation about a coping mechanism that I've had my entire life, which was staying quiet.
sentences.zh: 在演讲前，我们针对我一生都有的一种应对机制——保持安静，做了一个方案。

sentences.en: Staying quiet has kept me safe.
sentences.zh: 保持安静保护了我的安全。

sentences.en: And I kind of observed that as my therapist was reading my timeline.
sentences.zh: 当我的治疗师在读我的时间线时，我观察到了这一点。

sentences.en: And something shifted.
sentences.zh: 有什么东西改变了。

sentences.en: The really cool part about LA is we can't always detect.
sentences.zh: LI最酷的部分在于，我们并不总能察觉到。

sentences.en: We almost can never detect, actually, when the shift occurs, because it is so subtle.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们几乎永远无法察觉转变是何时发生的，因为它是如此微妙。

sentences.en: But the presentation was the following week, and 1,200 people showed up, and I spoke for 30 minutes, and I was fine.
sentences.zh: 但演讲是在第二周，1,200人出席了，我讲了30分钟，我很好。

sentences.en: And I had never done that in my life, ever, before.
sentences.zh: 我这辈子从来没有这样过。

sentences.en: And I got done, and I was like, hmm, I'm very suspicious.
sentences.zh: 结束之后，我想，嗯，我对此感到非常怀疑。

sentences.en: That's when I was still kind of new to LA myself, and I was like, there's no way.
sentences.zh: 那时候我自己对LI还算比较陌生，我就想，这不可能。

sentences.en: And I know that not every story is that magical, but for me, that was, it felt unreal.
sentences.zh: 我知道并不是每个故事都那么神奇，但对当时的我和我而言，感觉很不真实。

sentences.en: I feel that a shift that huge could take place, and me not even recognize it, right?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这么巨大的转变发生了，而我甚至都没有认出来，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, I call it behind-the-scenes therapy, because we can't see it.
sentences.zh: 就像，我称之为幕后疗法，因为我们看不见它。

sentences.en: We have no idea what's happening, because it's such a quiet process.
sentences.zh: 我们完全不知道发生了什么，因为它是一个如此安静的过程。

sentences.en: And it is, you know, it can be a little bit slower and a little bit more subtle, but that was not subtle for me at all.
sentences.zh: 它是，你知道，可能会慢一点，也更微妙一点，但这对我来说一点也不微妙。

sentences.en: That was the opposite of subtle.
sentences.zh: 那完全相反。

sentences.en: I just had no idea what was happening.
sentences.zh: 我只是不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: So, that was a big one.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个很大的转变。

sentences.en: Thanks for sharing that, Pamela.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你分享这个，帕梅拉。

sentences.en: That's great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah, and we are out of time, but just a couple of things I wanted to throw in.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们的时间到了，但还有几点我想插话。

sentences.en: You know, if you're thinking about considering a lie, like, you know, kind of informed consent about therapy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你正在考虑LI，就像，你知道，关于治疗的知情同意。

sentences.en: It's like, it is a hard process.
sentences.zh: 这就像，这是一个艰难的过程。

sentences.en: It can be very challenging.
sentences.zh: 它可能非常具有挑战性。

sentences.en: It has brought up a lot of things that I maybe didn't consciously remember or connect with,
sentences.zh: 它唤起了很多我可能没有有意识地记住或联系起来的事情，

sentences.en: and it has challenged me to face things that are very uncomfortable, as does any therapy, especially trauma therapy.
sentences.zh: 它挑战我去面对那些非常不舒服的事情，就像任何治疗一样，尤其是创伤治疗。

sentences.en: But I can absolutely say it, as it sounds like Kristen and Pamela would also, is that it is worth it.
sentences.zh: 但我绝对可以说，就像克里斯汀和帕梅拉听起来也会同意的那样，这是值得的。

sentences.en: It is worth the challenge.
sentences.zh: 这是值得挑战的。

sentences.en: It is worth some of the pain to get through the other side, to really experience some of that freedom.
sentences.zh: 为了到达另一端，为了真正体验那种自由，承受一些痛苦是值得的。

sentences.en: And yeah, Kristen mentioned nightmares.
sentences.zh: 是的，克里斯汀提到了噩梦。

sentences.en: Just a couple of things that I noticed people really spark to get some relief from pretty quickly is nightmares.
sentences.zh: 人们很快就能从中得到缓解的少数几个明显点就是噩梦。

sentences.en: You know, increased auto response, feeling tense, keyed up and on edge, just so those sort of states that are, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，自动反应增加、感到紧张、高度警惕和如坐针毡，只是那些，你知道的，

sentences.en: our systems is sort of, for a lot of us, have sort of existed in survival for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 对我们很多人来说，我们的系统在某种程度上已经在生存状态中存在了很长时间。

sentences.en: If not, since we were created in the womb, some of us have really been in that survival state from day one.
sentences.zh: 如果不是从我们在子宫里被创造出来开始，我们中的一些人从第一天起就真的处于那种生存状态。

sentences.en: And so it really does help to start to settle a lot of those little things that are just brought up because our system is just trying to keep us safe.
sentences.zh: 因此，它确实有助于开始平静许多那些因为我们的系统只是试图保护我们而引发的小问题。

sentences.en: Because we're able to recognize that present safety.
sentences.zh: 因为我们能够识别出当下的安全。

sentences.en: Like Kristen said in the beginning, you know, we always end in the present moment.
sentences.zh: 就像克里斯汀在开始时说的，你知道，我们总是以当下结束。

sentences.en: So something that happened yesterday or today, something recent, and then you're right here with me in present time.
sentences.zh: 所以昨天或今天发生的事情，一些最近的事情，然后你就在当下这里和我在一起。

sentences.en: And that has been a really, you know, a great tool for a lot of my clients.
sentences.zh: 这对我的许多来访者来说，真的是一个，你知道，很好的工具。

sentences.en: I've even had clients who told me outside of session, they can actually kind of hear my voice going, and you're right here with me in the present time.
sentences.zh: 我甚至有来访者告诉我，在会谈之外，他们实际上能听到我的声音在说，你现在就在当下这里陪着我。

sentences.en: And like, they just recognize that safety.
sentences.zh: 然后，他们只是认出了那种安全感。

sentences.en: So I really think that, you know, of course, informed consent, like it's hard, but it's worth it.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的认为，当然，知情同意，这很难，但它是值得的。

sentences.en: It's 100% worth it.
sentences.zh: 百分之百值得。

sentences.en: Anything else anyone wants to have before we wrap up?
sentences.zh: 在我们结束之前，还有人想补充什么吗？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, so glad we could do this today, guys.
sentences.zh: 很高兴今天我们能做这个，伙计们。

sentences.en: And we appreciate everybody who's listening.
sentences.zh: 我们感谢每一个收听的人。

sentences.en: And you can check out our other blogs on Taproot Therapy Collective.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Taproot Therapy Collective上查看我们的其他博客。

sentences.en: And we'll see you again next week.
sentences.zh: 我们下周再见。

sentences.en: Bye, guys.
sentences.zh: 再见，伙计们。

sentences.en: Hey, guys.
sentences.zh: 嘿，伙计们。

sentences.en: I wanted to pop in here to give you a quick reminder that we do this podcast for free.
sentences.zh: 我想插播一下，提醒大家我们这个播客是免费制作的。

sentences.en: And there are significant expenses associated with it, including the biggest resource in my life right now, which is time.
sentences.zh: 其中涉及大量费用，包括我目前生活中最大的资源，那就是时间。

sentences.zh: 有一件真正能帮到我们，希望也能帮到你的事情，就是去看看我们的赞助商之一，Hardy Nutritionals。

sentences.en: Hardy is a vitamin company that I never encountered the advertising of.
sentences.zh: Hardy是一家维生素公司，我以前从未见过他们的广告。

sentences.zh: 我们一次又一次地听到许多患有难治性焦虑症和多巴胺障碍的人说，

sentences.en: like bipolar disorder and other things, that they had tried everything, and Hardy was what worked.
sentences.zh: 比如双相情感障碍和其他问题，他们尝试过一切方法，而Hardy是起作用的。

sentences.en: And so I checked them out.
sentences.zh: 所以我去了解了他们。

sentences.en: And they have really good research.
sentences.zh: 他们的研究做得很好。

sentences.en: I'm not a fan of a lot of the BS that's in the supplement and wellness space.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢补充剂和健康领域的很多废话。

sentences.en: Hardy paid for a lot of research on their product.
sentences.zh: Hardy为他们的产品资助了大量的研究。

sentences.en: And when I ordered some for myself, I saw a big difference in my life.
sentences.zh: 当我为自己订购了一些时，我看到了生活中的巨大变化。

sentences.en: And my wife made fun of me, thought it was going to be Alex Jones selling vitamins on the radio.
sentences.zh: 我妻子还嘲笑我，以为会是亚历克斯·琼斯在收音机里卖维生素。

sentences.en: And when she tried them, she really liked them, too.
sentences.zh: 当她尝试了之后，她也非常喜欢。

sentences.en: There's a lot of data about how they can reduce the symptoms of ADHD without medications or lower your need for medication,
sentences.zh: 有很多数据表明它们如何在没有药物的情况下减少ADHD（注意力缺陷多动障碍）的症状，或降低你对药物的需求，

sentences.en: also manage some of the effects of autism spectrum disorder, and a whole lot of other things.
sentences.zh: 还能控制自闭症谱系障碍的一些影响，以及许多其他事情。

sentences.en: Newer research around nutrition is saying that the synergistic effects of multiple things being planned to work together is a lot more effective than one thing working alone.
sentences.zh: 关于营养的最新研究表明，多种事物协同起作用的协同效应比单一事物单独起作用要有效得多。

sentences.en: You can get a lot of information about that on our website.
sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站上获得很多相关信息。

sentences.en: Or you can head over to Get Hardy, that's G-E-T-H-A-R-D-Y, and use offer code TAPROOT for 15% off.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以前往Get Hardy，也就是G-E-T-H-A-R-D-Y，使用优惠码TAProot可享受85折优惠。

sentences.en: It would help them, it would help me, and it also would probably help you.
sentences.zh: 这会帮到他们，会帮到我，也可能会帮到你。

sentences.en: One of the more frequent things that patients and people in the randomized controlled trials that Hardy conducted report
sentences.zh: 患者和Hardy进行的随机对照试验中的人们报告的较为频繁的事情之一

sentences.en: is that they feel more themselves, more focused, and more effective at getting things done, which can result in all of us having a little bit more time.
sentences.zh: 是他们感觉更像自己了，更专注了，在完成事情时更有效率，这可以让我们所有人都多出一点时间。
